<table border="0" align="center" style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0;" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
  <tr>
    <td>
  <p>
Normally all the occurences for a level are retrieved and placed in an internal table before
the processing takes place.<br>
When this table is processed PAD knows for example when it is handling the last Occurence.<br>
The below example with the <b>{sequence:range}</b> tag does do that:
</p>
</td>
  </tr>
</table>



<p>

    </tr>

<b>{<font color="blue"><font color="purple">property</font><font color="black"><b>:</b></font>first</font><font color="red"></font>}</b>  X <b>{/<font color="blue"><font color="purple">property</font><font color="black"><b>:</b></font>first</font><font color="red"></font>}</b>  &lt;/td&gt;<br>          &lt;td&gt; <b>{<font color="blue"><font color="purple">property</font><font color="black"><b>:</b></font>last</font><font color="red"></font>}</b>   X <b>{/<font color="blue"><font color="purple">property</font><font color="black"><b>:</b></font>last</font><font color="red"></font>}</b>   &lt;/td&gt;<br>          &lt;td&gt; <b>{<font color="blue"><font color="purple">property</font><font color="black"><b>:</b></font>border</font><font color="red"></font>}</b> X <b>{/<font color="blue"><font color="purple">property</font><font color="black"><b>:</b></font>border</font><font color="red"></font>}</b> &lt;/td&gt;<br>        &lt;/tr&gt;<br>      <b>{/<font color="blue"><font color="purple">sequence</font><font color="black"><b>:</b></font>range</font><font color="red"></font>}</b><br>    <b>{/<font color="blue"><font color="purple">content</font><font color="black"><b>:</b></font>myTable</font><font color="red"></font>}</b></code></pre><!-- END DEMO SOURCE --></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><code><span style="color: #000000"><!-- START DEMO RESULT --><table border=1>

<table border="0" align="center" style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0;" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
  <tr>
    <td>
  <p>
  But some PAD tags use the PAD construct 'walking', then the occurences are processed one by one.<br>
  The tags <b>{pad:while}</b> &amp; <b>{pad:until}</b> are an example of this.<br>
  This 'walking' construct breaks those special pad tags like <b>{pad:last}</b> & <b>{pad:border}</b> that give information about a <b>{type:tag}</b><br>
  Also the 'Data Handling' options are broken since those work on the all occurences at once.
</p>
</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<table border="0" align="center" style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0;" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">

    <td>
  <p>
  To solve above breaking, place the result of a walking tag into the Data Store, and use it as a own tag.
</p>
</td>
  </tr>
</table>
